title: Detached window.setTimeout/clearTimeout breaks the debounced save in every real browser
detail: Production auto-init calls initBrowser() with env=window, so t.set/t.clear are window.setTimeout invoked with this={set,clear}; browsers throw TypeError: Illegal invocation (WebIDL brand check) on every rt:form-step-changed. Debounced save never schedules; only the pagehide beacon persists. Node tests pass arrow-function fakes, hiding it.
recommended_fix: Bind the receiver: set: function (fn, ms) { return env.setTimeout(fn, ms); }, clear: function (id) { env.clearTimeout(id); } — same for the root default. Add a wiring test whose fake env methods assert receiver shape.

title: Migration header still documents lazy token minting and row-removal erasure, contradicted by round-2 fixes
evidence:
--   * Erasure — the continue email carries a self-service delete link
--     (POST /apply/:code/draft-erasure/:token) that removes the row.

-- continue_token is 288 bits of URL-safe entropy (wisp.random_string(48)),
-- same capability model as application.erasure_token: the token IS the
-- auth. Partial unique index — most rows have NULL (token minted lazily on
-- the first "email me a link" request).
detail: Contradicted in-PR: upsert_application_draft.sql states 'The continue token is minted at SAVE time' (W1), so most rows are NOT NULL; erase_draft_by_token.sql states 'tombstone, NOT a hard delete' (W3). The schema file's own header misleads future readers on the GDPR model.
recommended_fix: Migration is unmerged: edit the two comment blocks in place to say tokens mint at save (COALESCE keeps existing) and erasure tombstones via erased_at until the retention sweep.
